study type: Retrospective cross-sectional study of archived samples
cohort: The study analyzed 99 human placental tissues previously collected and archived at the Duke University Medical Center from 2009 to 2015, from mothers with a mean age of 30.6 years, where 8% of newborns were characterized as low birthweight.
finding: Placental PBDE concentrations generally decreased over time, BDE-100 levels were significantly higher in female infant placentas, and placental BDE-47 concentrations were significantly associated with lower birthweight among male, but not female, infants.
birth_weight: 8% of newborns were characterized as low birthweight (<2500 g)
